text:
sarah-support: Heads-up — customer reports embeddings shape flip after they pinned a model. Reported vector length used to be 768, now they're intermittently getting 1024 when using the pinned variant.

nidhi-customer: Confirming — our client calls POST /v1/embeddings with model=pinned:acme:v2.1-quant, batching 8. No code change on our side; started after the pinned swap yesterday.

sarah-support: Minimal repro they gave:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings \n -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \n -d '{"model":"pinned:acme:v2.1-quant","input":["a","b","c","d","e","f","g","h"]}'
```
Response snippet: first embedding length 1024 (unexpected). They say single-item requests still return 768.

nidhi-customer: sample response from our app (trimmed):
{"data":[{"embedding":[0.001, 0.002, ..., <1024 values>],"index":0}, ...]}

deploy-bot: routing note: pinned variant substitution observed at 2026-03-17T21:04:12Z — routed pinned:acme:v2.1-quant -> v2.1-int8-compat due to capacity fallback on region-us-west-2.

james-ml: My immediate suspicion: the fallback/variant has a different embedding head (different vector_size). Batched requests might be routed differently (batch routing pool) and hit the fallback variant.

rafal-eng: Can you paste the trace ids + request ids? Also we need the model_metadata for both v2.1-quant and v2.1-int8-compat (embedding_size field).

sarah-support: Added the request ids to ticket #3456 (trace: trace-0a1b2c, reqs: r-9981..r-9988). Customer confirmed: single-item requests -> 768, batch 8 -> 1024.

james-ml: Repro suggestion: from support infra run the same batch sizes against the same pinned model in our staging region. If we can reproduce, check routing logs to see model_id per request. Also check if KV-cache/prefix caching could cause memory layout mismatch after quantization (unlikely to change dim but worth checking).

rafal-eng: Quick check on model manifests shows: v2.1-quant.metadata.embedding_size=768, v2.1-int8-compat.metadata.embedding_size=1024. So indeed the fallback has a different output dim.

nidhi-customer: So customer pinned an alias, but routing replaced it with a compat build that doesn't match expected head size? They specifically pinned 'acme:v2.1-quant' not compat.

rafal-eng: Looks like autoscaler-provisioning swapped some batched traffic to a different capacity pool that hosts the compat build. That pool advertises a different model_id. We need to prevent variant substitution for pinned contracts.

james-ml: Short-term mitigation options: 1) force the routing layer to honor exact model_id for pinned customers (disallow fallbacks), or 2) on detect, reject requests where returned embedding_size != pinned.expected_embedding_size with a clear error. I'd prefer (1) for enterprise pinned tenants.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-20260317-ACME-EMBED (assigned rafal-eng). Priority: P1 for customer-facing break.

rafal-eng: I'll push a hotfix to routing: if request.customer_has_pin then require exact model_id match (no compatibility substitution). Will schedule a rollback window after deploy. Also will backfill a check that logs embedding_size declared by model at allocation time.

alex-sales: FYI — customer is on reserved capacity + enterprise SLA. They're asking for rollback to the previous pinned commit until fix is validated.

sarah-support: I've told customer we'll either rollback or pin exact model commit for them. I've attached the request ids and repro. Working with ops on the rollback now.

james-ml: Follow-ups: add an alert when actual embedding_size != expected for pinned tenants (counts as regression); add a unit test that verifies model substitution never changes API contract for pinned requests.

rafal-eng: Deploying the routing hotfix to staging now, will test with batch=1 and batch=8 to confirm deterministic model_id.

sarah-support: Thanks all — will update ticket #3456 and ping CSM. If ops needs an immediate rollback, ping me. :thumbsup:
